Fit the model to draws of the detection histories

Source: R/fp_occu_mc.R
fp_occu_mc.Rd

Fits fp_occu() to each of several versions of the same data, which differ only in which occasions count as detections, and pools the posterior draws in equal shares. The versions are typically detection histories drawn from the posterior of a calibration of the classifier, as sheepdog::history_draws() produces, so that the uncertainty about which detections are true reaches the occupancy estimates (Monte Carlo propagation).

Usage

fp_occu_mc(
  data_list,
  ...,
  seed = NULL,
  parallel = FALSE,
  max_rhat = 1.05,
  keep_fits = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_mc'
summary(object, prob = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.fp_occu_mc'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_mc'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_mc'
as_draws_df(x, ...)

Arguments

data_list

A list of fp_data objects with the same sites, one per draw of the detection histories.

...

Arguments passed to fp_occu() for every fit (formulas, priors, sampler settings).

seed

Optional integer: fit i uses seed seed + i - 1. The fits are reproduced draw for draw only with one thread per chain (threads_per_chain = 1, the setting when parallel = TRUE).

parallel

Fit the versions in parallel with 'furrr', on the workers set by future::plan(). Unless set in ..., parallel_chains and threads_per_chain are then 1, so that each worker uses one core.

max_rhat

Fits whose largest R-hat exceeds this value are left out of the pooled draws, with a warning that names them. Inf keeps every fit.

keep_fits

Keep the fp_occu() fit of every version in the result (fits)? They hold the backend objects and can be large. Their draws are in memory, but with parallel = TRUE the CmdStan output files of a worker may be gone once it ends.

object, x

An fp_occu_mc object.

prob

Width of the equal-tailed intervals.

digits

Digits to print.

Value

An object of class fp_occu_mc: draws (the pooled draws, in the readable names of fp_occu(), the chains of fit i following those of fit i - 1), summaries (the posterior summary of each fit), diagnostics (one row per fit that ran: number of draws, divergences, largest R-hat, smallest bulk and tail effective sample sizes, and kept), fits (with keep_fits = TRUE, the fits kept), n_fits (the fits in the pool), and call.

summary() returns, for each quantity, the pooled posterior mean, standard deviation and interval, the standard deviations within and between fits (sd_within, sd_between), the share of the variance between fits (share_between), and the largest R-hat and smallest bulk effective sample size over the fits.

Details

What the pooled posterior is. Each fit conditions on one version of the detection histories; pooling the fits in equal shares averages the posterior over the versions. When the versions are draws from the posterior of a calibration, this approximates the posterior that accounts for the uncertainty of the calibration, but the calibration itself is not updated by the occupancy model (a "cut" model): information about the state of a site does not flow back to how likely its detections are to be true.

Between and within. summary() splits the posterior variance of each quantity into the part within fits (uncertainty given one version of the histories) and the part between fits (uncertainty about the histories), by the law of total variance: the squares of sd_within and sd_between add up to the variance of the pooled draws. A large share between fits means that the result depends on which detections are taken as true. The between part includes the Monte Carlo error of each fit's mean, which is small next to it unless the fits are short.

Failed fits. A version whose fit stops with an error is left out with a warning; the versions should weigh equally, so the function also warns when the fits have different numbers of draws.

Convergence. R-hat over the pooled draws would mix differences between fits with lack of convergence, so it is not reported for the pool. Each fit is checked on its own: a fit whose largest R-hat exceeds max_rhat (1.05 by default) has not converged and is left out, with a warning; report how many were left out. This is looser than the 1.01 that fp_occu() warns about, because mixing error within one fit mostly widens the within-fit part of the pooled variance; fits between the two values are kept, and their warnings show in diagnostics. Divergent transitions do not exclude a fit. Leaving fits out conditions the propagation on the versions that converged: if non-convergence depends on the version (for instance, histories with very few detections), the pooled posterior is biased and the between-fit variance understated. Rather than dropping them, refit those versions with longer chains or a higher adapt_delta. The summary reports the largest R-hat and the smallest effective sample size over the fits kept, and diagnostics lists every fit, with kept marking those in the pool.

Number of versions. The cost is that of one fit times the number of versions. The between-fit variance is estimated from the versions, so it needs several of them; check that the estimates of interest are stable as versions are added.

Experimental

This function is experimental (new in 2.0.0, part of the integration with 'sheepdog'): its arguments, its class and methods, and its results may change in a minor version. See crywolf-api.

See also

fp_occu(), fp_read_sheepdog()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# three versions of a simulated dataset, with detections switched off at
# random as if they had been judged false
sim <- simulate_fp(nsite = 100, nocc = 8, seed = 1)
versions <- purrr::map(1:3, function(i) {
  d <- sim$data
  set.seed(i)
  hit <- d$auto$y == 1
  d$auto$y[hit] <- stats::rbinom(sum(hit), 1, 0.9)
  d
})
mc <- fp_occu_mc(versions, occ = ~ x, fp = ~ 1, random_recorder = FALSE,
                 threads_per_chain = 1, seed = 1)
summary(mc)
} # }
